To post a few casual thoughts, I'm not sure that migrating to a similar site is a solution. What do you think? It's hard to make a community investment when you're building your house on sand each time and having to migrate every few years when it collapses, taking nothing with you. The days of having a personal blog connected to everyone through RSS were stronger in that regard. Increasingly I'm more resistant to sacrifice quality/independence for expedience/consolidation.

In the past I've avoided most platforms for that reason, although I am active on Twitter, which until photos were added was not very time consuming and probably a little more fun for writers. r/books was another exception, both as a reader and a writer, although since it went default the comment quality and some of the removals by mods has lead to my not enjoying it so much. I never found a film sub there that I really clicked with, unfortunately. r/movies was way too superhero religious and nothing else hit my film version of a Goldilocks CHZ like books pre-default did. Maybe there will be something that clicks here.

If anyone wants to be Goodreads friends or otherwise, please say hi. I do like to track what I'm reading and see what others are into. (Plus, as a non-famous author/filmmaker, I can't really not be on it!) Anyway, it's probably smart to connect in as many places as possible, given that ships go down and we're scrambling for rally points.

Does anyone know if VOAT allows for overwriting and deletion of comments? I didn't see anything about it in the site materials, such as the privacy policy. Did I miss that point?

I know my thoughts are a bit of a mixed review of community platforms, but I'll be around to see how it goes here and I wish everyone here the best. :-D
